title: The 5 Longest Snakes Alive, Ranked (The Anaconda Is Only #5)

scenes.text: The five longest snakes alive, ranked by the longest measured specimen. The anaconda only makes number five.
Number five: the green anaconda. 5.21 metres, reliably measured. The heaviest snake on Earth, not the longest.
scenes.label: Green anaconda · 5.21 m

scenes.text: Number four: the king cobra. 5.71 metres, at London Zoo in 1939. The longest venomous snake ever kept.
scenes.label: King cobra · 5.71 m

scenes.text: Number three: the Burmese python. 5.74 metres, a captive named Baby, measured in Illinois in 2016.
scenes.label: Burmese python · 5.74 m

scenes.text: Number two: the African rock python. Wild snakes over 6 metres are considered reliable, one from Gambia about 7.5.
scenes.label: Rock python · about 7.5 m

scenes.text: Number one: the reticulated python. Medusa, 7.67 metres and 159 kilograms, measured in Kansas City in 2011. A wild one hit 7.22 metres this January.
scenes.label: Reticulated python · 7.67 m

description:
The five longest snakes alive today, ranked by the longest reliably measured specimen.
The green anaconda is the heaviest snake but its longest reliable measurement is 5.21 metres; a king cobra at London Zoo reached 5.71 metres by 1939, the longest venomous snake on record; a Burmese python called Baby measured 5.74 metres in Illinois in 2016; wild African rock pythons over 6 metres are considered reliable, with a Gambian specimen of about 7.5 metres regarded as authentic; and the reticulated python Medusa measured 7.67 metres and 158.8 kilograms in Kansas City in 2011, the longest snake ever verified by Guinness World Records, while a wild female measured 7.22 metres in Sulawesi in January 2026.
Which snake would you have put at number one?
first_comment: Which would you put at number one? Old reports claim 8 to 10 metre anacondas and rock pythons, but none was ever verified. What should we rank next?
